posts:
ACT hides which 18 schools face 5% budget cuts, citing 'psychosocial risk' for principals instead of transparency.
Evidence: budget cuts, hidden lists, bureaucratic secrecy
#Education #ACT #Aletheia 🌐

The ACT government frames upcoming public school budget adjustments as a managed transition while withholding which specific schools face cuts.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +0.5) — Inclusive Active Capacity

Officials refuse to publish the 18 targeted schools, weaponizing 'psychosocial risk' to shield themselves from backlash while support staff are let go.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Systemic Erasure

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.
Bureaucratic opacity weaponizes staff well-being pretexts to mask funding cuts from the public.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 8.5, z: 3)

- ACT Education Dept: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Hides school cuts behind psychosocial pretexts.
- Public Schools & Staff: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Bears funding reductions without transparency.
While overall ACT school funding rises, 18 schools face 5 percent cuts by 2027, sparking intense community concern over transparency and support staff.

The Poison:
Hiding school cuts under the guise of protecting principals' mental health weaponizes legitimate workplace safety concerns to evade political accountability.

Plane Error:
Confusing bureaucratic public relations (WHO is embarrassed) with institutional duty (WHAT resources students actually receive).

Social Physics Analysis:
Officials run a classic Smart Selfish maneuver. Instead of owning budget cuts transparently, they project fear of criticism onto principals as a psychosocial shield to suppress dissent.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
Modal Dynamics: will be -> is not via Red Top (The Imperial Trap).
Promising equitable adjustments while hiding cuts crosses into exclusive erasure.

The Unavoidable Truth: Hiding budget cuts from affected communities breeds profound distrust.
The Unavoidable Lie: Concealing school names protects staff rather than politicians.

Alethekanon:
Invoking workplace safety to justify institutional secrecy is an inverted perversion of duty. Transparency is the bedrock of democratic accountability.

Awwthekanon:
Principals and teachers carry heavy burdens under tight budgets, and it hurts when authorities use their well-being as an excuse to avoid hard truths.

Brothekanon:
Wild that they think keeping school cuts secret helps anyone. Parents and teachers deserve to know what's coming instead of being left in the dark.

Spirithekanon:
"Let your speech be yes, yes; no, no." Matthew 5:37 FAIL
Masking policy cuts behind the rhetoric of care is deceitful double-speak that destroys community trust.

Actual Article Body:

The ACT government has announced that the budgets of 18 public schools will be cut by at least 5 per cent in 2027, while 22 schools will receive budget increases of at least 5 per cent.

Login or signup to continue reading

But the government is refusing to say which schools will receive less or more money.

Individual school budgets for 2027 have been published but the government declined to disclose how much funding schools received in 2026.

Education Minister Rachel Stephen-Smith said releasing the information would pose a psychosocial risk to principals.

"What we have seen over this period has been an identified psychosocial risk for individuals and principals, being identified," she said.

"With those schools being identified as having particular challenges around staffing or around budgets, and individual school principals having to go back to their communities to correct misinformation that has been provided to and through the media."

Ms Stephen-Smith suggested schools could save money through measures such as reducing extracurricular activities or combining some year 11 and 12 subject classes.

Overall schools in the Tuggeranong Valley would receive more funding.

"There's only one region where schools will be seeing an overall across the region slight reduction in funding. That's in the north and Gungahlin,'' Ms Stephen Smith said.

The government will provide16 schools with top-up or "exceptions funding" in 2027 to help them adjust to the new funding model.

Some public schools began letting go of learning support assistants earlier this year after being advised their budgets would be cut.

Education Director-General Jo Wood said the schools that would get less money would receive support from her directorate, including around occupational violence risk.

"They will be supported with supports from the education directorate, specifically through the programs that already exist, including around occupational violence risk and the adjustment space resourcing funding, and the funding that supports Aboriginal health,'' Ms Wood said.

Overall, funding to ACT schools will increase by 7.3 per cent in 2027.
